title: The interim settlement cycles bootstrap by deeming most calculations agreed rather than disputable
content:
A.2.4.1.2.1.5.2 through A.2.4.1.2.1.5.4 apply the same device three times. For the July/August 2025 cycle, Operational Executor Agent Amatsu's Initial Calculation covers only Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives, those amounts go through "the normal resolution process," and "For all other calculations, the amounts in the Independent Calculation will be treated as Agreed Amounts." For September 2025 the narrow scope is Spark. For November/December 2025 the roles invert — the Independent Calculation covers only Spark and everything else in the Initial Calculation is deemed agreed.

The pattern is a deliberate reduction in scope: rather than run a full adversarial settlement across every line item before the machinery is proven, each cycle exercises the dispute process on one product line and accepts the rest by construction.

This is a reasonable way to commission a process — the contested path gets tested on a real case each month while the volume flows through unimpeded — and it is only sound because the true-up mechanism exists. An amount deemed agreed can still be corrected in a later cycle under A.2.4.1.2.1.4, so deeming is a deferral of scrutiny rather than a waiver of it.

The accompanying schedule slippage is stated plainly and worth noting as evidence of load: A.2.4.1.2.1.5.1 makes the first cycle cover two months, and A.2.4.1.2.1.5.4 cancels the December 2025 cycle so that January 2026 again covers two months. A monthly clock that has skipped a beat twice in its first six cycles is a signal about the cost of the reconciliation work rather than about the design.
description: For each early cycle only one product line runs the full dispute process while all other amounts are treated as Agreed Amounts by fiat, shrinking the contested surface to what the process can handle.
